title: Araxys
description: A team workspace with real-time chat, live co-edited docs and an AI knowledge base that answers questions from your own docs, files and channels, with clickable sources.
highlights: Built channels, threads, DMs, presence, unread counts and notifications over Socket.IO, plus live co-editing of rich-text docs with Yjs (shared cursors; offline edits sync on reconnect) and comment threads.

Shipped a RAG knowledge base: a BullMQ/Redis worker chunks and embeds docs, uploaded PDFs/CSV/Markdown and public channels; MongoDB Atlas Vector Search answers with numbered, clickable citations, and private channels and DMs are never indexed.
Multi-tenant workspaces with owner/admin/member roles and invite links, an audit log with CSV export, full workspace export, and HMAC-signed webhooks to Slack/Discord with retries.
Rebuilt in seven phases from a v1 prototype: auth on every route and socket, zod-validated config, and 228 API tests (unit + integration on an in-memory MongoDB) running in CI.
Runs on a self-hosted Android phone (PM2 + Cloudflare Tunnel, frontend on Netlify) with CI-gated push-to-deploy, health checks and automatic rollback.

tldr.problem: Teams keep knowledge in scattered docs and chats, then re-ask the same questions.
tldr.build: One workspace for chat, co-edited docs and a RAG knowledge base, with a BullMQ ingestion worker and per-workspace vector search.
tldr.result: Cited answers from the team's own content, 228 automated API tests, and push-to-deploy onto a self-hosted phone server.

title: AVMG
description: An all-in-one media toolkit: download from almost any site, convert formats, compress a video to fit an upload limit, clean up audio, grab frames, quick-edit, and pull subtitles without downloading the video.
highlights: Designed a distributed video transcoding pipeline (FFmpeg + BullMQ workers) with job pickup latency under 500ms.
Implemented subtitle harvesting via yt-dlp metadata-only fetches, cutting per-video transfer from ~400MB to under 1MB.
Built a live job dashboard that streams transcode progress to users, with automatic retries for failed jobs.

Serves finished files straight from disk: a zero-copy rename plus streamed, resumable (HTTP Range) downloads replaced a cloud upload that read whole videos into RAM, and lifted the old 50 MB free-tier file cap.
Self-hosted on an Android phone: moved Prisma to its Rust-free client (its native engine has no Android build) and apply migrations from the deploy pipeline with psql.

Added six ffmpeg tools on the same queue: compress-to-size (bitrate fitted from duration), loudness and silence cleanup, frame grabs and contact sheets, rotate/flip/speed edits, a subtitle fetcher and an instant media inspector. Every option is whitelisted before it reaches ffmpeg, and encodes are CPU-capped.

tldr.problem: Converting and archiving media meant juggling several tools, and long transcodes blocked everything behind them.
tldr.build: A BullMQ + FFmpeg worker pipeline with Redis queues, live job telemetry, metadata-only subtitle fetches, and files served straight from the server's disk.
tldr.result: Job pickup under 500ms, per-video transfer cut from ~400MB to under 1MB, and no RAM spike or file-size cap on delivery.

title: Warden
description: Paste a YouTube lecture and get revision notes that follow the video as it plays, then flashcards and an OMR-style answer sheet built from the same lecture. Every card and question links back to the moment it came from.
highlights: Go API and Go worker that never call each other: jobs live in Postgres, and each step (captions, notes, flashcards, quiz) is saved with its own marker, so a crash or retry only reruns what's missing and a lecture someone already made returns in milliseconds with no AI call.

Treats Gemini's output as untrusted input: Go checks every timestamp is a real transcript line, every quiz has four distinct options and a real answer, and every "asked in the exam" mark quotes the teacher's actual words, with one fix-up call before failing.
No AI SDK: plain HTTP from Go to Gemini, with retries when Google is busy and a clean stop when the daily quota runs out.
Next.js study screens: notes synced to the embedded YouTube player with a highlighter sweep, focus mode, flip-card flashcards and an answer sheet scored +4/-1 like the real NEET paper.
Own auth, daily limits, NEET and General templates, a library and a Revise tab, covered by Go integration tests and Playwright end-to-end tests.

tldr.problem: Watching a lecture feels like learning more than it is, and making notes and practice questions by hand takes longer than the lecture.
tldr.build: A Go pipeline that turns captions into checked notes, flashcards and a quiz, saved step by step in Postgres, and a Next.js site that syncs them to the video.
tldr.result: Notes that follow the video, practice tied to exact timestamps, and AI output that is verified in code instead of trusted.

title: Gutter
description: A Chrome side panel that reads the AI chat you have open (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or Grok) and answers side questions about it, so the main thread stays clean.
highlights: Manifest V3 extension (React + TypeScript) that reads the open chat with per-site selectors served by the backend, so fixes ship without a store review.
Three ways to answer: Chrome's on-device Gemini Nano (free, nothing leaves the computer), hosted models through the Gutter server, or the user's own API key.

A hybrid router picks between lookup and explain answers: a semantic matcher first, the on-device model only on near-ties. It scored 90/100 in a bake-off against 87 (semantic only), 86 (Nano only) and 59 (rules).

Long chats: code picks the parts that match the question by words and by meaning, each answer lists what it was based on, and "second opinion" checks the last answer with a model from a different company.
Express + MongoDB server for accounts, synced side notes and per-account free limits, self-hosted on an Android phone with CI-gated deploys.

tldr.problem: Asking a side question in an AI chat derails the main thread you were working in.
tldr.build: A side panel that reads the open chat and answers on the side, on-device or through hosted models, with a routed lookup/explain answer style.
tldr.result: Side questions that never pollute the main chat, free on-device answers, and nothing sent to the main chat without the user's say.

title: Pocket Server
description: An Android phone turned into a production server: Termux runs the backends for Araxys, AVMG and Gutter plus their databases, published through a Cloudflare Tunnel, with push-to-deploy from GitHub.
highlights: Runs 10 PM2-managed processes on one phone (three app backends and their workers, PostgreSQL, Redis, cloudflared and a deploy service) and brings them all back after a reboot.
One Cloudflare named tunnel routes four hostnames to local ports: no open ports and no public IP. Frontends are on Netlify.

Push-to-deploy: after CI passes, GitHub Actions sends an HMAC-signed, timestamped request; the phone fast-forwards only to commits already on main, installs, migrates, reloads PM2, health-checks and rolls back on failure, and the log shows up in Actions.

Worked around Android-specific breakage: compiled bcrypt on-device with node-gyp, moved Prisma to its Rust-free client, applied migrations without Prisma's engine, and pointed yt-dlp at Node for YouTube's JavaScript checks.

tldr.problem: Hosting several side projects on cloud VMs costs money every month for very little traffic.
tldr.build: A phone running every backend under PM2 behind a Cloudflare Tunnel, with a signed deploy webhook driven by GitHub Actions.
tldr.result: Three live backends for the cost of electricity, deployed on every green push, with automatic rollback.

title: KnowYourPolitician
description: An open data pipeline on Indian politicians: election history since 1962 joined to self-declared criminal cases, assets and education from ECI affidavits, with party-wise analytics.
highlights: Built a reproducible Python pipeline (download, canonical SQLite, scrape, entity matching, analytics) holding 449K politicians, 575K candidacies since 1962, 155K affidavits and 87K criminal-case records.
Matches MyNeta affidavits to Lok Dhaba candidates exact, then fuzzy, then a human review queue, so uncertain matches are never guessed.
Scrapes only public statutory disclosures, politely: identified User-Agent, at least 2 seconds between requests, and an on-disk HTTP cache so reruns never hit a server twice.
Editorial rules in code: pending cases are never called convictions, nobody is labelled corrupt (ADR-style percentages only), and every fact keeps its source URL and scrape time.
A Next.js front end for politicians, parties and cases.

tldr.problem: Voters can't easily see a candidate's election record next to what they declared in their affidavits.
tldr.build: A cached, throttled scraping and matching pipeline that joins Lok Dhaba election data to ECI affidavits in one SQLite database.
tldr.result: Six decades of candidacies linked to declared cases, assets and education, with sources kept for every fact.

title: KropiGo
description: A freelance agri-marketplace connecting kisan (farmers) directly with buyers — farmers list produce, buyers purchase, and admins oversee the entire marketplace.
highlights: Built real-time order and listing updates with Socket.io across a MERN/Next.js stack.
Used RTK Query to keep marketplace listings and orders fast and in sync on the client.
Implemented role-based access control (RBAC) and multi-tier admin workflows for kisan, buyers, and admins, including marketplace moderation.
Optimized image delivery with Cloudinary transformations and lazy loading, improving page load performance on low-bandwidth connections.

tldr.problem: Farmers selling produce lose margin to middlemen and have no direct line to buyers.
tldr.build: A Next.js/MERN marketplace with Socket.io live listings, RBAC across kisan/buyer/admin roles, and moderation workflows.
tldr.result: Direct farmer-to-buyer sales with real-time order updates, and Cloudinary-optimised images for low-bandwidth rural connections.

title: SolarVistar
description: A freelance CRM build for SolarVistar, a company based in Khargone, MP — giving their team a central place to manage leads, customers, and day-to-day operations.
highlights: Delivered a full CRM on a MERN stack with RTK Query for efficient, cache-aware data fetching.
Modeled relational customer and operations data in PostgreSQL with Prisma.
Integrated Cloudinary for media uploads and asset management across the platform.
Shipped the project end-to-end as a freelance engagement, from requirements to deployment.

tldr.problem: A solar company in Khargone was running leads, customers, and daily operations out of spreadsheets.
tldr.build: A full MERN CRM with RTK Query caching, relational data modelled in PostgreSQL via Prisma, and Cloudinary media handling.
tldr.result: Delivered end-to-end as a solo freelance engagement — requirements through deployment — giving the team one system of record.

title: WatchThis
description: An AI-driven movie recommendation platform that suggests films tailored to your taste, lets you save them to a personal watchlist, and surfaces rich details on every title.
highlights: Generated personalized movie recommendations and surfaced detailed metadata via the TMDB API.
Built a persistent, user-specific watchlist backed by Firebase.
Crafted a responsive React front end for browsing, searching, and saving titles.
Designed detail views covering cast, ratings, synopsis, and related recommendations.

tldr.problem: Picking something to watch means bouncing between reviews, trailers, and half-remembered recommendations.
tldr.build: A React app on the TMDB API with AI-driven suggestions, rich detail views, and a Firebase-backed personal watchlist.
tldr.result: One place to discover a film, dig into cast and ratings, and save it for later.
